summary: A concise overview of this week's technology developments, focusing on advancements in artificial intelligence, privacy-centric mobile operating systems, and the legal complexities of model training.

items.title: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything. Will everyone use them?
items.summary: OpenAI is actively developing AI agents designed to assist with a wide range of tasks from software engineering to everyday activities. This initiative represents a major push to bring autonomous agent technology to mainstream users.

items.title: Hugging Face reportedly in talks to be acquired for $13B
items.summary: Hugging Face is reportedly discussing potential acquisition offers that value the open-source AI platform at approximately $13 billion. However, the founders' commitment to the community has raised doubts about whether a sale will ultimately go through.

items.title: Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha?
items.summary: A mysterious new AI model named Ox Alpha has emerged in stealth, sparking intense speculation across the tech community. Its sudden appearance highlights the ongoing competitive frenzy and secrecy surrounding frontier model development.

items.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
items.summary: The legal implications of training AI models on copyrighted books remain highly complex and contested. This debate is crucial as authors raise concerns about their work being used without consent to build tools that could threaten their livelihoods.

items.title: De-Googled GrapheneOS is coming to Motorola’s foldables next year
items.summary: GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused and de-Googled version of Android, has announced plans to officially support Motorola smartphones starting next year. This expansion brings advanced security features to a wider range of hardware, including foldable devices.
